title: GitHub Copilot: The World's Most Widely Adopted AI Developer Tool

primary.label: Coding Agents & Software Engineering

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk is centered on GitHub Copilot as a coding assistant across IDE and GitHub.com, covering codegen, chat, PR summaries, and code modernization. GitHub Copilot is a widely adopted coding assistant product for developers. Copilot is in production with enterprise features launched, and audience adoption is discussed. The talk targets developers new to Copilot, emphasizing prompt crafting takes under an hour to learn. The presentation combines slide narration with pre-recorded and live product demonstrations. All claims are directly stated in the transcript by the speaker.

summary: Dave Bernes, a Senior DevOps Advocate at GitHub, delivers a talk on GitHub Copilot's history and expanding capabilities at the AI Engineer World's Fair in San Francisco. He traces Copilot's evolution from initial code generation in the IDE (Copilot Individual), to Copilot Business, then Copilot Chat enabling richer pair-programming interactions, and Copilot Enterprise launched in February, which extends Copilot to GitHub.com for PR summaries, knowledge base queries, Bing search integration, and repository indexing. Copilot works across VS Code, GitHub Codespaces, JetBrains IDEs, and Visual Studio regardless of where code is stored. Dave shows a demo video of building Django/Python models using natural language comments, where Copilot generates class definitions contextually. He highlights that Copilot is a pair programmer, not an autopilot—developers must review and refine suggestions. He stresses prompt crafting: specificity in comments yields better suggestions, and learning it takes under an hour. Copilot Chat is demoed explaining undocumented regex code, refactoring for readability, proposing bug fixes, and generating unit tests. Copilot Extensions announced at Microsoft Build bring third-party services like Octopus Deploy into Copilot Chat. In the live Enterprise demo, Dave shows knowledge base queries producing specific framework guidance (FlipperFR for feature flags), repository-indexed code search finding sales tax calculation code, Bing-powered API discovery (Avalara for sales tax), Copilot generating updated code with security best practices (storing API keys in HashiCorp Vault or Azure Key Vault), and automated PR summaries with file-by-file change descriptions. He also demonstrates PR code change explanations for reviewers and notes Copilot works with any language including COBOL, suggesting it as a modernization tool. Dave shares a training resources URL and directs attendees to the GitHub booth for more information including Copilot Workspace.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Copilot Evolution
sections.summary: Dave introduces himself and surveys audience adoption of Copilot. He traces the product evolution from Copilot Individual for code generation, to Copilot Business, Copilot Chat for richer interactions, and Copilot Enterprise launched in February for GitHub.com integration with PR summaries and knowledge base queries.

sections.title: Copilot Basics Demo and Prompt Crafting
sections.summary: A video demo shows building Django/Python models from natural language comments, with Copilot generating classes contextually. Dave emphasizes Copilot is a pair programmer not an autopilot, highlights the need for developer review when Copilot allowed unwanted deletions, and discusses prompt crafting specificity for better results.

sections.title: Copilot Chat Demo
sections.summary: A demo video shows Copilot Chat explaining undocumented regex code, refactoring for readability, proposing bug fixes by comparing comments to code, and generating unit tests. Dave notes Copilot is constrained to programming questions and will decline off-topic queries.

sections.title: Copilot Extensions and Octopus Deploy Demo
sections.summary: Dave covers Copilot Extensions announced at Microsoft Build, bringing third-party services into Copilot Chat. An Octopus Deploy demo shows querying deployment dashboards without leaving the IDE. Dave cuts the demo short to cover remaining topics.

sections.title: Copilot Enterprise Live Demo: Knowledge Bases and Repository Search
sections.summary: Dave live-demos Copilot Enterprise on GitHub.com, querying knowledge bases for feature flag guidance and receiving specific framework recommendations (FlipperFR). He switches to an Enterprise Managed Users environment with a Parts Unlimited repo, uses repository-indexed search to find sales tax calculation code and its callers, and uses Bing search to discover public sales tax APIs like Avalara.

sections.title: Copilot Enterprise Live Demo: Code Generation with Security Guidance and PR Features
sections.summary: Dave asks Copilot to rewrite the calculate tax function using the Avalara API, receiving updated code plus security guidance about storing API keys in HashiCorp Vault or Azure Key Vault. He then demos PR summary generation with file-by-file change listings and PR code change explanations for reviewers.

sections.title: Language Support, COBOL Modernization, and Wrap-up
sections.summary: Dave notes Copilot works with any language including COBOL, demonstrating COBOL code explanation and suggesting translation to Java or C as a modernization approach. He mentions Copilot Workspace but runs out of time, shares a training resources URL with 15-20 links, and directs attendees to the GitHub booth for more information.
